title: The Famous Door hires Ben Webster to play Dixieland
summary: With bop everywhere, the Famous Door wants a Dixieland band, so Ben borrows arrangements and rehearses at Eddie Barefield's studio with Buck Clayton and Bennie Morton.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Now to a wonderful era in my life, we'll get to Ben now, Ben Webster. Just a few weeks after being at the Deuces with Don Byas, Ben Webster wanted to know if I'd like to go into the Famous Door, he was going in to the Famous Door with a band, and I don't know how to explain this -- but he had some arrangements. The Famous Door wanted to be different from the other clubs on the Street, there was so much bop going on and everything was happening, bop was being flown then.
And The Famous Door wanted something a little different, so they asked Ben if they wanted to come in with
a Dixieland band. I don't think anybodie that hears this or any musician was aware of what was happening then. And if they hear this interview, they will certainly get a laugh out of it.

Anyway, Ben borrowed some Dixieland arrangements from somebody, and we went in and we went to rehearsal, which was up in Eddie Barefield's studio on 48th Street -- and the band personnel started out, Buck Clayton on trumpet, Bennie Morton on trombone, Eddie Barefield, and Ken Kersey. However, I have to say first, as we went to the rehearsal, he hadn't hired Kenny yet and we rehearsed first, without Kenny, and somebody suggested that Monk --Thelonius Monk -- was at Linton's and he was out for awhile and he could use a job.

Excuse me for interrupting again, Cliff. But I think for the record we might as well let them know that the studio you were rehearsing in was Eddie Barefield who was a saxophone player. And the piano player - and Ken Kersey was a pianist so they would know who Ken Kersey was -- he was a pianist, the late Ken Kersey, and of course, everybody knows he played piano. Please carry on.
